key_insight: ScienceIDE turns scientific code repositories into programmable environments that AI agents can learn from directly. In simple terms, it converts scattered research code into structured, testable training grounds for scientific reasoning and tool use.
problem_solved: The paper addresses the 'scientific experience bottleneck': scientific code is rich with knowledge, but it is hard for AI to learn from because toolchains are fragmented, domain conventions are implicit, and correctness criteria are highly specialized.
method: Builds infrastructure that wraps scientific code into agent-learnable environments.
Uses expert-defined scientific guidance to define tasks, rules, and evaluation criteria.
Standardizes interaction with scientific repositories so agents can explore, execute, and learn in a more reliable way.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, ScienceIDE offers a path to train agents on real scientific workflows instead of synthetic toy tasks. This could improve scientific coding assistants, automated experimentation, and agentic systems that work with domain-specific tools and research software.
visual_elements: Pipeline diagram showing scientific code repositories transformed into agent environments

paper_title: ScienceIDE: Turning World's Scientific Codebase into Agent Learnable Environments
paper_authors: Hejia Geng, Zesen Huang, Haoyang Li, Wenbin Li, Koutian Wu
